results: Physical continuous restriction to the CLOSED original unit interval is a bounded linear map of norm at most ONE and preserves EVERY original point, including both traces.

The ACTUAL zero-potential Dirichlet source contour projector is uniformly bounded by TWO in both physical L2-to-continuous and L2-to-L2 norms, and fixes the literal original free sine. This is derived from the PROVED exact physical sine kernel and its unnormalized bilinear mass ONE HALF; no orthogonality assumption is supplied.

For ANY complex continuous periodic F with F(0)=0 and ANY physical L2 Fourier data H, the original two-mode Fourier approximation produces a literal unit-interval sine vector within TWICE the original uniform error. Its coefficient is explicitly 2*i*FourierCoefficient(H,n); the correction is controlled by the ACTUAL zero trace, with no assumed cancellation or unit energy for approximate Fourier coefficients.

For the IDENTICAL physical interval restriction, the ACTUAL Dirichlet projection error is bounded by its ACTUAL free-projection operator error times the interval norm, plus SIX times the ACTUAL periodic two-mode uniform error. This follows from the literal sine fixed vector, not an abstract replacement for either contour projection.

The ENTIRE original endpoint norm ball has COMPACT image in EVERY admissible lower finite-p original distribution space. Applied to the SAME original H-minus-one distribution and compact native extraction image, this gives ONE cutoff BEFORE ALL complex period-one sources in EACH original endpoint norm ball for actual Dirichlet source-circle validity, same-index isolation and algebraic multiplicity ONE.

The ACTUAL Dirichlet source projections converge to the ACTUAL free projections UNIFORMLY on EACH fixed ORIGINAL endpoint norm ball, in ALL THREE original L2-to-continuous, L2-to-essential-supremum and L2-to-L2 operator norms. No supplied compactness, convergence or normalized eigenfunction hypothesis is used in this convergence theorem.

The ACTUAL continuous periodic Riesz projector fixes the SAME H1 representative of EVERY physical spectral-range vector. Combining actual periodic and Dirichlet convergence gives interval projection error STRICTLY LESS THAN ONE HALF for EVERY norm-one zero-boundary vector in the ENTIRE actual high periodic spectral range, including ALL complex associated directions.

Source (32) is PROVED with its EXACT final constants: for EVERY actual normalized Dirichlet eigenfunction v and EVERY norm-one zero-boundary actual periodic spectral vector G with its faithful unit-norm native interval representative g, the ACTUAL projection equals nu*v and ONE HALF <= norm(nu) <= THREE HALVES. ONE original endpoint norm-ball cutoff precedes q, n, G, g and v and may exceed ANY supplied prior cutoff.

Actual G and g satisfying the required boundary, full spectral-range, original stronger-entire-distribution and EXACT physical norm-one properties EXIST at the SAME uniform cutoff and satisfy the PROVED overlap. The paper-specific phase-fixed formula is not needed for this stronger all-vector overlap statement.

Full native weak operator restriction compatibility, actual spectral-basis coefficient decomposition, corrected FULL projected identity (31), full Lemma2.15, full COMPLEX weighted midpoint2.1(ii), quantitative Dirichlet C.4(ii), remaining low periodic parity/interlacing and actual Birkhoff/KdV constructions remain OPEN. source_correspondence.potential: ENTIRE original complex FourierLebesgueSpace(2,-r,infinity),0<=r<1/2, with physical period ONE. No reality or zero-mean premise is added.
source_correspondence.contours: Both ACTUAL source circles have literal original center(pi*n)^2 and radius n, with the same original positive index n.
source_correspondence.normalization: Periodic physical L2 uses probability Haar = one-half integral[0,2]. Interval physical L2 is UNNORMALIZED integral[0,1]. The prior parity/domain theorem gives BOTH norms EXACTLY ONE for the SAME continuous function.
source_correspondence.boundary: The zero trace at zero controls the sum of the two ACTUAL Fourier coefficients. Their approximate sum is not asserted to vanish identically, and their energy is not asserted to be exactly one. An explicit boundary correction gives a nearby literal sine vector.
